case.case_title: Bandara and Another v. Premachandra, Secretary, Ministry of Lands, Irrigation and Mahaweli Development and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 213/93, decided on 8th, 9th and 23rd June 1993

clause.text: Freedom to form and join a trade union.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioners' dismissal for participation in trade union activities violated their fundamental right to freedom to form and join a trade union under Article 14(1)(d).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed their dismissal was due to their trade union membership and activities, protected under Article 14(1)(d).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued the dismissal was justified due to misconduct and probationary status, and that the 'pleasure principle' allowed dismissal without reason.
key_facts: Petitioners were appointed on probation and joined the Government Surveyors’ Association, a registered trade union.
They participated in a work-to-rule campaign and submitted sick notes for absence.
The 2nd respondent informed them their services were terminated due to trade union participation.
Petitioners gave a written undertaking to refrain from trade union activities during training to be reinstated, but were not reinstated.
The court found the dismissal was not by proper authority and violated fundamental rights.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 14(1)(d) protects the right to form and join trade unions and engage in lawful trade union activities. However, this right is not absolute and may be limited by misconduct or other lawful disciplinary grounds.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the petitioners were dismissed primarily for their trade union participation, not misconduct. The Establishments Code and constitutional provisions require fairness and non-arbitrariness in dismissal, even under probation. The dismissal violated Article 12(1) equality rights and was discriminatory.
principles_established: Trade union rights include protection from dismissal for participation in lawful activities.
Dismissal under probation must follow fair procedures and just cause under the Establishments Code.
The 'pleasure principle' of Article 55(1) is subject to constitutional limitations including equality and fairness.
Discriminatory dismissal without rational basis violates Article 12(1).

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioners were improperly dismissed for their trade union participation, violating their fundamental rights under Article 14(1)(d) and Article 12(1). They were entitled to reinstatement with seniority and compensation.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Reinstatement with effect from 7.12.92, arrears of salary from 21.12.92, retention of seniority, and Rs. 2,000/- compensation each.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The petitioners' dismissal was directly due to their trade union membership and activities, implicating their right under Article 14(1)(d). The court's reasoning and relief were centrally based on protecting this constitutional right against arbitrary dismissal.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: It is quite clear that the purported dismissal of the Petitioners was on account of their participation in trade union action, and not on account of any misconduct or considerations therewith. The fundamental rights under Article 12(1) have been violated, They are entitled to reinstatement and to resume their course of studies forthwith, retaining seniority over students subsequently admitted to that course of studies.
